record.paper_title: Toward epidemic thresholds on temporal networks: a review and open questions
record.original_question: Small-scale local structures in a temporal contact network, such as unusually dense subgraphs, anomalous cliques, or chain-like patterns, can strongly alter how infection propagates. How can techniques for detecting such local structures be connected to epidemic-threshold analysis, and how exactly do those local structures affect disease dynamics on temporal networks?

evidence.quote: Local structures, i.e., interaction patterns localized to a small part of the network, can play a significant role in the transmission of a diseases through the network.
Connecting these detection techniques to epidemic thresholds and understanding the impact of local structures on disease dynamics is an important open question.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let a temporal network be a sequence $G = (V, E_1, E_2, \ldots, E_T)$, where $V$ is a fixed finite set of nodes and each $E_t \subseteq \binom{V}{2}$ is the set of contacts active at discrete time step $t$. Consider a Susceptible–Infected–Susceptible (or SIR) compartmental process on $G$ with per-contact infection probability $\beta \in (0,1]$ and per-step recovery probability $\mu \in (0,1]$; the epidemic threshold is the critical value $(\beta/\mu)_c$ separating the regime where an initial infection dies out almost surely (in the large-network limit) from the regime where it persists with positive probability.

Define a "local structure" in $G$ to be a small subset $S \subseteq V$ together with the induced temporal subgraph $(S, E_1\cap\binom{S}{2}, \ldots, E_T\cap\binom{S}{2})$ exhibiting one of the following patterns: (i) an anomalously dense temporal subgraph (more contacts among $S$ across time than expected under a chosen null model), (ii) a temporal clique (a subset $S$ in which every pair is in contact at least once within a time window $\Delta$), or (iii) a temporal chain (a sequence of nodes $v_1, \ldots, v_k$ with contacts $\{v_i, v_{i+1}\}$ active at strictly increasing times $t_1 < t_2 < \cdots < t_{k-1}$).

Problem. Develop a rigorous framework that:

(a) connects algorithmic detection of local structures of types (i)–(iii) to the computation or bounding of the epidemic threshold $(\beta/\mu)_c$ on temporal networks, producing explicit upper and/or lower bounds on $(\beta/\mu)_c$ as functionals of the detected local structures; and

(b) quantifies the effect of each type of local structure on the disease dynamics — for instance, by giving asymptotic expressions, in terms of the sizes, densities and temporal arrangements of these local structures, for the expected outbreak size, the time to extinction, and the shift of the epidemic threshold relative to a randomized null version of $G$ that destroys the local structure while preserving global statistics (such as aggregate degree distribution and contact rate).
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (2020–2025) studies temporal motifs, temporal cores, and community detection in temporal networks, and separately derives epidemic thresholds via contact-based models, but a general framework explicitly linking detection of local structures (dense subgraphs, temporal cliques, chains) to epidemic-threshold computation and quantitative effects on disease dynamics has not been established. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Relevance of temporal cores for epidemic spread in temporal networks
status_evidence.snippet: Studies how dense temporal cores influence epidemic spreading, but does not provide a closed-form connection to the epidemic threshold.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on linking dense local temporal structures to spreading, but no general threshold framework.

status_evidence.title: A powerful lens for temporal network analysis: temporal motifs
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) survey of temporal motifs as local structures; emphasizes motif detection but treats epidemic-threshold connections as future work.
status_evidence.claim: Detection techniques are advancing, yet their integration with epidemic thresholds remains an open direction.

status_evidence.title: A systematic framework of modelling epidemics on temporal networks
status_evidence.snippet: Provides modelling frameworks for epidemics on temporal networks but does not resolve the role of arbitrary local structures in setting thresholds.
status_evidence.claim: General framework still does not pin down quantitative effects of local structures on thresholds.
